content.intro: {state} does not charge sales tax on vehicles. It charges a one-time title ad valorem tax of {stateRate} of the vehicle's value when you title it, plus a title fee and a yearly registration fee.

howItWorks.text: The tax is {stateRate} of the fair market value, paid once when the vehicle is titled. For a new vehicle the value is the higher of the selling price or the state schedule value. For a used vehicle it is the value in the state assessment manual.
At a dealer, a trade-in lowers the taxable value, and so do rebates and dealer discounts on a new vehicle. In a private sale the trade-in does not count.
People who move to the state and bring a vehicle pay a lower rate, and transfers between family members pay a much lower one. The calculator uses the standard rate.
The title fee is charged once and registration is renewed every year. Electric vehicles pay an additional yearly fee that the state publishes each July.

faq.q: Is there sales tax on a car in Georgia?
faq.text: No. The title ad valorem tax takes its place and is paid once when the vehicle is titled.

faq.q: Is the tax based on the price I paid?
faq.text: Not always. For a used vehicle it is based on the state's assessed value, which can differ from the price. For a new vehicle it is the higher of the price or the state value.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the tax?
faq.text: Yes when a dealer makes the sale. It does not in a private sale.

faq.q: Do I pay the yearly local vehicle tax too?
faq.text: Vehicles titled under this tax do not pay the yearly local ad valorem tax, though that tax still applies to vehicles that are not titled this way.
Yes. They pay an extra yearly licensing fee, published by the state each July.
